sections.content: How many people are "aircraft maintenance and related trades"?

18,165 people

were counted on the census as "aircraft maintenance and related trades" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Aircraft maintenance and related trades fit, service, repair and overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "aircraft maintenance and related trades" there were more men than women (95.6% compared with 4.4%).

This means "aircraft maintenance and related trades" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 95.7% and women made up 4.3% of "aircraft maintenance and related trades"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "aircraft maintenance and related trades" included:

  • window cleaners
  • metal machining setters and setter-operators
  • taxi and cab drivers and chauffeurs

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "aircraft maintenance and related trades" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "aircraft maintenance and related trades", 12.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "aircraft maintenance and related trades" was 65 years or older.

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "aircraft maintenance and related trades", 5.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (95% compared with 5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.6%) than self-employed (6.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Flintshire, this is in Wales.
